answer:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded answer to "What types of plant introductions were influenced by urban land use?")

"Unintentionally introduced plants (accidental arrivals with contaminated seed lots, trade and tourism) are the introduction type most strongly influenced by urban land-use CHANGE in the Barcelona province plots: their plot-level richness increases with urban expansion measured over the surrounding landscape (urban-cover gain at 500–1000 m buffers, both 1956–2009 and 1993–2009), consistent with urban-driven disturbance and dispersal corridors. In contrast, gardening-introduced species — although they dominate the recent regional influx (75.2% of all post-1985 first records in Catalonia) — show no positive association with urban land cover at any year or buffer scale, and are even slightly negatively associated with very recent local (50 m) urbanization; agri-forest introductions show no detectable association with urban cover or urban change at any scale. Urban land-use LEVEL per se is a weak predictor: unintentional species were historically tied to the rural/cropland matrix (negative coefficients on 1956/1993 urban cover at 1000 m, positive on 1993 cropland), so it is the progressive urbanization of the landscape over time, not standing urban cover, that relates to unintentional introductions."

EVIDENCE (all values observed in the executed analysis; n=632 plots; Poisson count models with habitat (10 levels, ref. Broad-leaved forests), elevation, temperature, rainfall, radiation, distance.road, distance.stream as controls; NB2 escalation triggered only if Pearson dispersion >1.5, which never occurred — dispersions 0.59–1.19):

Part A — level models (27 pathway × year × scale models; results/models_urban_cover.csv):
- No urban-cover coefficient survives FDR(BH) across the 27-model family.
- Nominal signals: n.unint ~ urban.1956.1000m = −1.39 (SE 0.58, p=0.016); ~ urban.1993.1000m = −0.96 (p=0.020); n.unint ~ cropland.1993.50m = +0.41 (p=0.047). n.gard and n.agfo: no nominal urban effect anywhere (|p|≥0.06; n.agfo coefficients unstable, SE up to 6.4, only 9 source species).
- Moran's I on residuals: n.gard ≈0, n.agfo ≈0; n.unint I=0.04–0.06, permutation p≈0.005–0.015 → material spatial autocorrelation for the unintentional model → cluster-robust variant computed (Part D).

Part B — change models (results/models_change.csv, models_prog_regr.csv):
- n.unint ~ urban delta 1993→2009 at 500 m: +1.72 (p=0.0064); at 1000 m: +2.09 (p=0.032); urban delta 1956→2009 at 500 m: +1.13 (p=0.019). At the 50 m scale the same delta is null/negative (−0.13 to −0.34, ns).
- n.unint ~ progressive.1993.2009.50m = +0.54 (p=0.036), progressive.1956.2009.50m = −0.22 (ns) — mixed across periods.
- n.gard ~ urban delta 1993→2009 at 50 m = −0.89 (p=0.031); all other n.gard urban terms null. n.agfo: all null (smallest p=0.09).
- FDR across the Part B family (24 urban terms): none survive at q<0.05; across the 12 change-category terms: none survive.

Part D — spatially robust variants (cluster-robust SE by 95 ten-km UTM grid cells; results/models_cluster_robust.csv):
- n.unint ~ urban delta 500 m (1993→2009): coef +1.72, p stays 0.0079; 1956→2009: p=0.0139; 1000 m (1993→2009): +2.09, p=0.0466 — the urban-expansion association for unintentional introductions is robust to spatial clustering.
- n.gard ~ urban delta 50 m (1993→2009): −0.89, p=0.0268 — also survives clustering.
- The negative LEVEL effects (urban.1956/1993.1000m) weaken to p=0.072/0.092 — suggestive, not confirmatory.

Part E — zeros and sensitivity (results/zeroinflation_check.csv, sensitivity.csv):
- Zero shares: n.gard 0.815 observed vs 0.803 Poisson-expected; n.unint 0.771 vs 0.733; n.agfo 0.967 vs 0.967 — near-Poisson, no material zero inflation; documented decision: plain Poisson count models retained.
- Dropping the 4 all-zero-change rows: n.unint ~ urban.1956.1000m coefficient −1.44 vs −1.39 (p=0.014 vs 0.015) — insensitive. Dropping the 441 plots with n.total=0: n.gard coefficient −0.27 vs −0.29 — insensitive.

Part F — species-level characterization (deduplicated 77 species; results/species_*.csv):
- Growth-form composition differs sharply: Unintentional 18/29 annual herbs (mean height 1.07 m, mean invaded plots 9.5, mean niche breadth 0.75); Gardening 17/41 shrub-trees and 18/41 perennial herbs (mean height 6.1 m, mean invaded plots 4.0, niche breadth 0.45); AgriForest 6/9 shrub-trees. Kruskal–Wallis on invaded.niche.breadth across pathways H=5.91, p=0.052 (borderline). This supports the mechanistic reading: unintentional urban-associated species are fast-spreading herbs, not planted ornamentals.

Part G — region-level corroboration, descriptive only (results/contingency_*.csv):
- Period × pathway χ²=230.4, df=6, p=6.3e-47; Gardening's share of new regional records rises 16.8% → 44.6% → 49.0% → 75.2% (Before 1500 → 1985–2019) while AgriForest falls 51.4% → 6.1%. Clearly labeled as temporal context for the regional species pool, NOT causal or plot-level evidence — and note it shows the gardening surge happened region-wide, which our plot models show is NOT explained by local urban cover.

WORKFLOW (executed in analysis.py; full log in results/summary.txt):
1) Plot-level table parsed (632 rows × 37 cols; row-wise pathway counts verified to sum to n.total in all rows).
2) 27 GLM count models (Poisson with dispersion check and NB2 escalation rule; NB2 never needed) for n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo vs urban + cropland cover at each of 1956/1993/2009 × 50/500/1000 m + controls; BH-FDR across the 27 urban coefficients.
3) Change models: (i) progressive/regressive proportions at 50 m (no.changes baseline), (ii) urban-specific delta (urban.Y1 − urban.Y0) plus cropland delta at all three scales, for both periods — attributing "progressive" change to urbanization vs the mixed category.
4) Moran's I (kNN k=8, 199 permutations) on every model's residuals; where material (n.unint), cluster-robust SEs by 10-km grid cell reported for all key coefficients.
5) Zero-structure check (observed vs expected zero shares) and two sensitivity refits (drop 4 zero-change rows; drop 441 n.total=0 plots).
6) Species-level characterization from the deduplicated 81→77-row trait table; Kruskal–Wallis across pathways.
7) Temporal contingency table: χ² and row-percentage trends, explicitly labeled descriptive context.
The phylogenetic tree was not used, as agreed.

LIMITATIONS / UNCERTAINTIES (carried into the hypothesis's wording):
- No urban term survives multiple-testing correction (FDR) across the full model family; the unintentional/urban-expansion link is nominal (raw p=0.006–0.047) but consistent in sign across both periods and both wide-buffer scales and robust to spatial clustering — hence stated as the main supported association, with moderate confidence.
- AgriForest conclusions are weak (9 source species, 0.04 mean count/plot): "no detectable association" ≠ "no association".
- "Progressive/regressive" categories mix urban and cropland change; the urban-specific delta models resolve this and give the same directional answer for n.unint, but the mixed-category coefficients themselves were unstable across periods.
- Plot counts are species richness per pathway (not abundance); a plot–species join table is not supplied, so the species-level table is used for characterization, not for direct linkage.
- Observational, correlational design: causal attribution to urban land use is not demonstrable from these data alone.

payload.hypothesis: Unintentionally introduced plants are the introduction type most strongly influenced by urban land-use change: their plot-level richness increases with urban expansion at 500-1000 m buffers over both 1956-2009 and 1993-2009 (robust to spatial clustering), while gardening-introduced species show no positive association with urban cover at any scale and agri-forest introductions show none detectable; urban land-use LEVEL is a weak predictor, the signal being with progressive urbanization of the landscape rather than standing urban cover.
payload.workflow: 632-plot count models (Poisson, dispersion-checked) for n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo vs urban+cropland at 3 years x 3 buffers with habitat/climate/distance controls; change-category (progressive/regressive) and urban-delta models at all scales; BH-FDR across 27+24 urban terms; Moran's I (kNN k=8, permutation) with cluster-robust SEs by 95 x 10-km grid cells; zero-structure and drop-row sensitivity; deduplicated (77) species characterization; contingency-table chi-square as descriptive context.
